neighbour_expectation.note: Leak case: candidate light fully mixed into the target aperture gives at most D*Fc/(Fc+Ft); in reality the target's optimal aperture holds only part of the candidate's light 11.5 arcsec (2.9 px) away, so less. On-target case: a target dip D_t leaking a fraction e of the target flux into the candidate photometry gives D_c = D_t*e*Ft/(Fc+e*Ft) < D_t, so D_t > 2165 ppm.

kic_only_source.note: KIC source with no 2MASS and no Gaia DR3 counterpart within 3 arcsec; the nearest Gaia source (2073896294004902144, G 19.77) lies 3.2 arcsec from the KIC position. Probably the same object with poor KIC astrometry/photometry, or a spurious KIC entry; Gaia should resolve a G~19 star 4 arcsec from a G 16.2 star.

notes: diff_centroid_* is the specified estimator (3x3 box around the brightest difference pixel by flux). Per quarter the brightest pixel is often a noise excursion in the target's core (its S/N is listed as brightest_diff_pixel_snr), so this estimator is bimodal; its bootstrap/MC covariance and the multi_quarter_mean_offset built from it are not reliable. snrbox_* uses the same 3x3 flux-weighted centroid boxed on the highest-S/N difference pixel.

two_source_fit uses a Gaussian PSF (not the Kepler PRF) with both stars at their Gaia/WCS positions; it is an approximate check, implied depth = fitted difference amplitude / fitted direct amplitude of the same star.
